name: Integration for Mailchimp – Contact Form 7, WPForms, Elementor, Gravity Forms and More
author: Plugcrux

sections.description:
This plugin sends form submissions from Contact Form 7, WPForms, Elementor Forms, Gravity Forms, and Formidable Forms to Mailchimp.

When a user submits a form, the plugin can add or update subscribers in your Mailchimp audience. This helps reduce manual data entry and keeps your Mailchimp lists in sync with your website forms.

Supported form plugins:

  • Contact Form 7
  • WPForms
  • Elementor Forms
  • Gravity Forms
  • Formidable Forms

Authentication

To connect your Mailchimp account:

  1. Go to Settings > Connections.
  2. Click Add Connection.
  3. Enter an identifiable name (for example, “Main Mailchimp Account”).
  4. Paste your Mailchimp API key. It is checked with Mailchimp before it is saved.
  5. Click Save connection. The connection is listed with a masked key.

If Mailchimp stops accepting a key, the connection is marked “Reconnect needed” and a notice appears at the top of the plugin. Edit the connection to paste a new key, or use Re-check once the key works again.

You can also add a connection while creating an integration; it is selected for you when you return to the wizard.

Add Integration

Integrations are created in a three-step wizard:

  1. Form and audience: enter a name, pick the form (Contact Form 7, WPForms, Elementor Forms, Gravity Forms or Formidable Forms), the Mailchimp connection and the audience. Test connection and Refresh from Mailchimp are available here.
  2. Field mapping: map form fields (or custom values) to Mailchimp merge fields. The Additional details section holds the subscription status, preferred language, email format, VIP status, a note and Mailchimp tags (pick an existing tag or type a new one).
  3. Record action and filters: choose a record action (Always create a new record, Create or update, or Update only) and, optionally, filter which submissions are sent.

Use Test run to send one sample subscriber and see Mailchimp’s response before you save.

Logs

The Logs page lists every record your forms send to Mailchimp, page by page.

  • Statuses: Success, Failed and Skipped (a submission that did not match the integration’s filter conditions).
  • Failed entries show the code Mailchimp returned. If a subscriber was saved but its note or tags could not be added, the entry is logged as NOTE_FAILED.
  • Filter by status, integration or message, search, and sort.
  • View a log to see the form data and Mailchimp’s response, including the result of the note and tags.
  • Resync or delete entries one by one, or use bulk actions.

Settings

Global settings can be managed from the Settings page:

  • Connections – add, rename, re-check and remove Mailchimp connections.
  • Notifications – email one or more addresses when a record fails, with your own subject line.
  • General – delete all plugin data when the plugin is deleted from WordPress.

External services

This plugin connects to Mailchimp to send your form submissions to your Mailchimp audience.

Mailchimp Marketing API (https://<dc>.api.mailchimp.com, where <dc> is the data center of your API key)

  • Used to: validate the API key, load audiences and merge fields, run Test run, and send form submissions and resyncs.
  • Data sent: the API key (for authentication) and the mapped form field values (email, merge fields, tags, notes).
  • Terms of Service: https://mailchimp.com/legal/terms/
  • Privacy Policy: https://mailchimp.com/legal/privacy/

Privacy and Data Handling

  • We do not collect any data from your site or your visitors.
  • Form submission data is sent only to Mailchimp.

Features

  • Connect supported form plugins to Mailchimp
  • Unlimited connections and integrations
  • Map fields, including name, phone, company, city, state, zip, country, email, address lines, birthday, custom values, system fields and Mailchimp custom merge fields
  • Additional details: subscription status, preferred language, email format, VIP status, note and Mailchimp tags
  • Record actions: Always create a new record, Create or update, Update only
  • Conditional filters to control which submissions are sent
  • Test run to check an integration before saving
  • Logs with Success, Failed and Skipped statuses
  • Resync entries one by one or in bulk
  • Email notifications for failed records
  • Option to delete all plugin data on uninstall

Support

If you need help or want to request a feature:

  • https://integrazo.com/pages/contact
  • https://integrazo.com/pages/request-feature

Website: https://integrazo.com
Email: support@integrazo.com

Additional Notes

This plugin supports WordPress multisite installations and has been tested for compatibility with recent WordPress versions.
sections.installation:
Automatic installation
1. Go to Plugins > Add New in your WordPress dashboard.
2. In the search bar, type Integrazo and locate this plugin.
3. Click Install and then Activate.
4. Go to the plugin settings to connect your Mailchimp account and start syncing.

Manual installation
1. Upload the plugin ZIP file via Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
2. Activate the plugin.
3. Go to the plugin settings and complete the setup.
sections.faq:
Which WordPress form plugins does this support?

This plugin currently supports:

  • Contact Form 7
  • WPForms
  • Elementor Forms
  • Gravity Forms
  • Formidable Forms

How do I integrate Contact Form 7 with Mailchimp?

  1. Open the plugin and go to the Setup tab.
  2. Choose Contact Form 7 as the form type.
  3. Select the Mailchimp audience.
  4. Map the Contact Form 7 fields to Mailchimp fields.
  5. Save the integration.

How do I integrate WPForms with Mailchimp?

  1. Go to the plugin’s Setup section.
  2. Select WPForms as the form type.
  3. Choose the Mailchimp audience.
  4. Map WPForms fields to Mailchimp fields.
  5. Save the integration.

The same general steps apply for Elementor Forms, Gravity Forms, and Formidable Forms: choose the form type, select the Mailchimp audience, map fields, and then save.

Can I map custom fields in Mailchimp?

Yes, you can map form fields to custom Mailchimp merge fields where available. This helps organize and segment your audience more effectively.

What happens if a submission fails to sync with Mailchimp?

Failed submissions are:

  • Recorded in the Logs section
  • Shown with the error message returned by Mailchimp
  • Available for manual or bulk resync

Do I need a Mailchimp account to use this plugin?

Yes. You need an active Mailchimp account to send data from your WordPress site to Mailchimp.

Is data transfer secure between WordPress and Mailchimp?

The plugin uses secure communication over HTTPS when your site and Mailchimp endpoints are configured to use HTTPS.

Is this a dedicated Mailchimp integration for WordPress forms?

Yes. It connects supported forms directly to Mailchimp without an external automation service.

Do I need an automation service to send form data to Mailchimp?

No. The plugin sends form data directly from your WordPress site to Mailchimp.
sections.changelog:
2.0.0

  • New: Completely redesigned admin interface – Setup, Logs and Settings.
  • Removed: The Form Filters sub-tab.
  • New: Three-step setup wizard with a Test run and a “Refresh from Mailchimp” button.
  • New: Record actions – Always create a new record, Create or update, and Update only.
  • New: Skipped entries are logged with the Skipped status.
  • New: Additional details section – subscription status, language, email format, VIP status, notes and Mailchimp tags (existing or new).
  • New: Logs record every sent, skipped and failed entry, load page by page, and show the response including the note and tags results.
  • New: Faster admin – tabs, editing an integration and actions work without page reloads, with background preloading.
  • New: “Reconnect needed” alerts, and a Re-check button on every connection.
  • New: Unlimited connections and integrations.
  • Improved: All audiences and all merge fields of your Mailchimp account are loaded.
  • Improved: Existing members get their tags through Mailchimp’s tags endpoint.
  • Improved: Secure API key handling – keys are checked, hidden in the interface and validated for their data center.
  • Improved: Dates and times show in your site timezone.
  • Improved: Security, performance and translation-readiness. Requires PHP 7.4.
  • Removed: The review notice, promotional banners and the list of other plugins.

1.0.15

  • Checked: Tested and confirmed compatible with WordPress 7.1.

1.0.14

  • Fixed: Missing spacing between the add (+) and remove (−) buttons in the field mapping table.

1.0.13

  • Security: Hardened admin AJAX endpoints with proper capability checks.
  • Security: Improved function naming consistency across admin action handlers.
  • Fixed: Translation wrappers added to user-facing admin notice strings.
  • Added: Help dropdown in admin header for quick support access.
  • Added: Deactivation feedback popup.
  • Added: Form Filters sub-tab under Settings.
  • Improved: Minor UI and code quality improvements.
  • Checked: Tested and confirmed compatible with WordPress 7.0.

1.0.12

  • Security: Added ABSPATH check to prevent direct file access across missing files.

1.0.11

  • Fixed: Settings link in Plugins page now uses admin_url() for improved compatibility.
  • Improved: Code hardening with stricter output escaping in admin views.
  • Checked: Tested and confirmed compatible with WordPress 6.9.1.

1.0.10

  • Improved: Readme content clarity and wording for better understanding of supported forms and Mailchimp integrations.
  • Updated: Short description to clearly mention support for other form submissions.
  • Improved: Minor UI text refinements across admin pages.

1.0.9

  • Changed: Replaced transient-based account authentication storage with WordPress options for improved reliability.
  • Improved: Better handling of authentication errors and session recovery.
  • Improved: Data sanitization and validation in the Accounts and Setup pages.
  • Fixed: Edge cases where account data could be lost during browser refresh or delayed redirects.

1.0.8

  • Checked: Plugin tested and confirmed compatible with WordPress 6.9
  • Updated: “Tested up to” value updated to 6.9 in readme.txt

1.0.7

  • Updated: Readme file revised to follow WordPress.org guidelines.
  • Updated: Description, tags, and sections rewritten for clarity and compliance.

1.0.6

  • Changed: Elementor Forms integration flow updated for smoother setup.
  • Improved: Better results and reliability when mapping Elementor form fields.
  • Added: Dismissible admin notice reminding users to reconfigure Elementor Forms after update.

1.0.5

  • Added: FAQ entry about disabling specific integrations.
  • Fixed: All known error notices reported by WordPress debug logs.
  • Checked: Tested with WordPress 6.8.2.

1.0.4

  • Fixed: Issue where some Mailchimp fields were not displaying properly.
  • Fixed: Elementor form listing method updated for better compatibility.

1.0.3

  • Added: Improved validation and sanitization.
  • Fixed: Issue causing a blank page when selecting a list.

1.0.2

  • Added: WordPress 6.8 compatibility.
  • Fixed: Removed unnecessary use of $wpdb->prepare() for static table names.
  • Fixed: i18n issue by removing an empty __() string in get_columns().

1.0.1

  • Verified: Compatibility with WordPress 6.7.2.
  • Updated: Applied recent Mailchimp API changes.
  • Refined: User interface adjustments.

1.0.0

  • Initial release with:
    • Support for Contact Form 7, Gravity Forms, WPForms, Elementor Forms, and Formidable Forms.
    • Error logging and retry features.
    • Email notifications for integration failures.
